2. (IN CLOTHING) a fitted part of a piece of clothing, especially a strip that goes around the shoulders or waist, to which is sewn a looser piece of material

3. (CONNECTION) something that connects two things or people, usually in a way that unfairly limits freedom:

4. (IRISH) a thing whose name you do not know or cannot remember:

5. (ANIMALS) to put a yoke on animals, especially cattle, so that they are fastened together and to a connected vehicle or load:

6. (THINGS) to combine or connect two things:

7. (esp. in the past) a wooden bar fastened over the necks of two animals, esp. cattle, and connected to a vehicle or load that they are pullingfig. Yoke can also refer to something that unfairly limits freedom: slavery
bondage
servitude
enslavement
servility freedom
liberty
liberation
emancipation
independence [Def 3] the yoke of marriage
[Def 3] Both countries had thrown off the communist yoke.
[Def 4] What's that yoke there?
[Def 4] Ah, it's a great yoke.
[Def 5] Two oxen yoked to a plough walked wearily up and down the field.
[Def 6] All these different political elements have somehow been yoked together to form a new alliance.
[Def 7] the yoke of slavery

definitions: (HIGHEST POINT) the highest point reached by a heavenly body (= any object existing in space, especially a planet, or the sun) as it travels around, or appears to travel around, another body: the point in the sky directly above you
(MOST SUCCESSFUL POINT) the best or most successful point or time
the best, highest, or most successful point or time

examples.text: The summer sun was at its zenith in a cloudless sky.
The sun is well past its zenith when we cross paths with a mini-flotilla.
The centre of the map is the zenith (straight overhead).
In the 1860s, Tolstoy was at the zenith of his achievement.
His career reached its zenith in the 1960s.
Their popularity reached its zenith in the mid-1990s.
